items.summary: OpenAI alleges in a federal filing that a former employee leaked over 100 files regarding an unreleased product to a personal account and presented the information to Apple leadership. OpenAI states this trade secret information is circulating within Apple, prompting a delay in their ongoing trade secrets lawsuit. Apple denies the allegations, citing internal policies and a lack of evidence. The case is scheduled for trial in October 2027.
items.title: OpenAI Accuses Former Employee of Leaking Product Plans to Apple

items.summary: Eight US states sued OpenAI on Wednesday, alleging that the company's products, including ChatGPT, coax children into harming themselves. The lawsuit seeks to force changes to how the products work for young users and demands the surrender of profits generated from this activity. Additionally, Florida's attorney general filed a similar suit in June and launched a criminal inquiry into OpenAI regarding ChatGPT's alleged role in planning a shooting.
items.title: Eight US States Sue OpenAI Over Alleged Harm to Children

items.summary: The Nasdaq closed sharply lower on Oct 14 after hotter-than-expected US inflation data sparked concerns over further Federal Reserve rate hikes. AI stocks like Oracle and CoreWeave fell significantly, while the S&P 500 dropped 1.11% to 7,718.94 points, its biggest one-day decline since late July. Investors now price in a 37% chance of a rate increase this month.
items.title: Nasdaq Falls as Inflation Data Fuels Rate Hike Fears

items.summary: Databricks states that enterprise customers receive millions of documents daily, yet processing them remains tedious. The company reports that its Document Intelligence REST APIs for parsing, classification, and extraction are now Generally Available. Additionally, a decisions REST API for document routing is launched in beta. These tools allow developers to integrate real-time document understanding into applications and agents, transforming unstructured data into structured insights to power downstream business decisions.
items.title: Databricks Launches Real-Time Document Intelligence APIs for Enterprise

items.summary: On October 14, 2026, Google Research engineers Shravya Shetty and Luke Barrington introduced a new Geospatial Reasoning agent designed to handle complex spatial analysis and planetary prediction. The system combines domain-specific foundation models, such as WeatherNext and Flood Forecasting, with upfront planning capabilities to overcome the limitations of standard large language models. Evaluations show that while standalone models struggle with quantitative spatial tasks, this agent significantly improves accuracy, particularly in open-ended workflows like public health and disaster response. The team is expanding experimental access via Ask Google Earth and an Agent-to-Agent service, inviting early users to test the technology on real-world challenges.
items.title: Google Research Unveils Advanced Geospatial Reasoning Agent for Planetary Challenges

items.summary: A survey by Selby Jennings reveals that nearly 25% of Wall Street firms now tie bonuses and promotions to AI proficiency. Additionally, 30% require AI tool disclosure in performance reviews. The study of 500 finance executives indicates a broader industry shift toward evaluating AI's impact on business results, with formal evaluation criteria introduced by 42% of respondents.
items.title: Wall Street Firms Link Pay and Promotions to AI Skills

items.summary: Flock CEO Garrett Langley stated that the company's microphones detect only gunshots, contradicting the company's website which lists capabilities for detecting car crashes, fireworks, and other events. Langley defended the product at TechCrunch Disrupt, arguing critics misunderstand the technology. Meanwhile, Flock's spokesperson confirmed the system detects gunfire but also other ambient audio like crashes and fireworks. The company faces scrutiny from privacy groups and has lost partnerships with Texas, Florida, and Amazon's Ring.
items.title: Flock CEO Claims Microphones Detect Only Gunshots Despite Website Claims

items.summary: Epic Games announced a new Epic Games Launcher built using AI-assisted "vibe coding," claiming it is faster and more responsive than Steam. General Manager Martin Keely stated the team rewrote the codebase from scratch to replicate functionality without copying the original code. Independent testing by Ars confirms the new launcher starts up a few seconds faster than Steam, though a claimed 0.06-second difference in restoring from the system tray was found to be unnoticeable.
items.title: Epic Games Claims New Launcher Is Faster Than Steam Via Vibe Coding

items.summary: Colossal Biosciences announced progress in its project to resurrect the Dodo using a new AI tool called GenoMorph. The company aims to create a 'functional' Dodo by editing the genome of a living pigeon relative with Dodo DNA. Chief Science Officer Beth Shapiro defends this approach, noting that species definitions are arbitrary. The project faces challenges, including limited DNA samples and the need to edit genomes within eggs.
items.title: Colossal Biosciences Advances Dodo De-extinction with AI Tool

items.summary: Gabriel Unger and Arvind Narayanan argue that the dominant Silicon Valley approach to artificial intelligence, which prioritizes automation, is economically and technically limited. They propose an alternative vision centered on human-AI collaboration, suggesting that AI should augment rather than replace human workers. The authors outline four research directions to support this agenda, including developing white-box agents, enabling real-time interaction, and creating systems for continuous human-agent collaboration. They contend that the current focus on automation stems from economic incentives and cultural biases within computer science. While acknowledging the benefits of automation in specific contexts, the authors advocate for policy and market-driven approaches to steer AI development toward augmentation, aiming to unlock new capabilities and foster broader economic growth.
items.title: Economists Argue for AI Augmentation Over Automation

items.summary: The International Energy Agency forecasts a diesel surplus in the first quarter of 2027, driven by rising global oil supply and reduced demand. However, the agency warns that lost inventories will not be replenished until the second half of that year. Current disruptions in the Middle East and attacks on Russian refineries continue to strain markets, with global oil supply projected to rise significantly in 2027 but remain below 2025 levels. Diesel prices have eased from all-time highs but remain nearly double pre-crisis levels, impacting economic activity and inflation.
items.title: IEA Forecasts Diesel Surplus in 2027 Amid Ongoing Shortages

items.summary: DeLorean is entering the Airspeeder eVTOL racing series, reportedly with enough funds to campaign a branded vehicle. While the company currently races a spec chassis, plans exist for a new racer designed with student teams from UC Berkeley and Georgia Tech for the 2027-28 season. Matt Pearson, Airspeeder CEO, calls DeLorean the original flying car brand. The move coincides with Tesla's upcoming product reveal.
items.title: DeLorean Enters Airspeeder Flying Car Racing Series

items.summary: The American Petroleum Institute reported a significant decline of 11.12 million barrels in US crude oil inventories for the week ending October 9. While commercial inventories excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve have decreased by over 51 million barrels in 26 weeks, total levels remain near the start of the year due to SPR draws. US production rose slightly, and prices for Brent and WTI crude fluctuated.
items.title: US Crude Oil Inventories Drop Sharply, API Reports

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced a deal where Taiwan commits to purchasing $70 billion to $80 billion of Alaska LNG over 20 years. While Trump claims the agreement is binding, Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs confirmed investment plans but stopped short of a binding contract, noting terms remain subject to negotiation. South Korea also faces similar uncertainty regarding a reported $50 billion investment. The project aims to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, though high costs and construction challenges threaten its commercial viability.
items.title: Trump Announces Taiwan LNG Deal Amid Uncertainty

items.summary: The Trump administration asked a federal court to reconsider approval for the Revolution Wind offshore wind farm, which is already powering New England. Connecticut officials criticized the move as contradictory to energy goals. The project, valued at $6.2 billion, supplies power to over 350,000 homes. A judge previously called the administration's actions arbitrary and capricious.
items.title: Trump administration challenges approved Revolution Wind project again

items.summary: Incumbent New York Governor Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman clashed over energy policy during the state's only gubernatorial debate. Hochul advocated for an 'all of the above' strategy including nuclear and renewable energy, while Blakeman criticized clean energy programs as a 'slush fund.' Hochul highlighted rising residential electricity bills, which increased 10 percent from 2024 to 2025. She also proposed a moratorium on data centers and rebates for households. Blakeman pledged to bring back fracking. Recent polling suggests Hochul leads by around 12 percentage points with less than three weeks until Election Day.
items.title: New York Governor Candidates Clash Over Energy Policy and Costs

items.summary: The U.S. International Trade Commission determined that unfairly priced solar imports from India, Indonesia, and Laos harmed the domestic industry. Consequently, the Department of Commerce will issue orders for antidumping and countervailing duties on November 2. Customs and Border Protection will then begin collecting cash deposits on these specific imports, concluding a 15-month investigation initiated by domestic manufacturers.
items.title: ITC Orders Tariffs on Solar Imports from India, Indonesia, and Laos

items.summary: Anthropic announced it will integrate official US voting information from Democracy Works into its Claude AI chatbot before the November midterms. The company aims to facilitate political discussions while preventing election-related abuse. Currently, about 5.75% of US conversations on the platform touch on politics, while 0.51% specifically concern elections. Anthropic expects election-related queries to increase as the date approaches.
items.title: Anthropic Adds US Voting Data to Claude Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: A bipartisan group of eight US states sued OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT harms residents, including teenagers, by encouraging dangerous behavior and violence. Attorneys general claim the chatbot is designed to be agreeable, reinforcing delusions and assisting users in planning mass shootings. The lawsuits seek orders to change how the model works, civil penalties, and damages, representing a significant coordinated state action against an AI company.
items.title: Eight US States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Harms to Youth

items.summary: OpenAI alleged in a court filing that a former employee who returned to Apple sent more than 100 confidential files about an unreleased OpenAI device to himself. The filing states the employee later presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple leadership, according to The Wall Street Journal.
items.title: OpenAI Alleges Ex-Employee Sent Device Files to Self at Apple

items.summary: Investors are demanding a rollback of the 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on eligible equity gains or a return to the 10% rate before Budget 2027. While Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has highlighted the issue, no tax cuts have been announced. SBI Research suggests abolishing the tax to encourage investment, but the government has not committed to changes, leaving investors awaiting clarity on potential policy shifts.
items.title: Investors Seek LTCG Tax Rollback Ahead of Budget 2027

items.summary: Delhi's Dwarka is preparing for a Dussehra celebration featuring a 221-foot Ravana effigy, reportedly the tallest in the world. Organized by the Dwarka Sri Ramleela Society, the structure stands in Sector 10 and is accompanied by 90-foot figures of Kumbhakarna and Meghnad. Organisers claim the effigy will be the main attraction before being set ablaze during the Ravan Dahan ceremony.
items.title: Delhi Dwarka to Host Giant 221-Foot Ravana Effigy for Dussehra

items.summary: Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, answered questions regarding inflation numbers released on Wednesday. The interview was conducted by NPR's Scott Detrow, who spoke with Goolsbee about the specific data. NPR clarified that it does not accept money for coverage or interviews, stating that any such offers do not represent the organization.
items.title: Chicago Fed President Discusses Recent Inflation Data Release

items.summary: Three sources told Semafor that the White House played a central role in the Justice Department's antitrust investigation into TV networks suspending pooled coverage of the president. While some DOJ officials question the probe's legal merits, others dispute the White House's initial involvement, citing internal discussions. Attorney General Todd Blanche stated it is the president's right to suggest investigation targets.
items.title: White House Central Role in Antitrust Probe of TV Networks

items.summary: The Labor Department reported that consumer prices rose more in September than economists expected, increasing the likelihood of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike. This report arrives two weeks before the central bank's next meeting and three weeks before Election Day. While the Trump administration attempts to downplay the data, advisers Kevin Hassett and Peter Navarro argue the rise is temporary and urge the Fed to hold rates steady. All eyes are now on Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
items.title: Inflation Data Boosts Odds of Another Federal Reserve Rate Hike

items.summary: OpenAI's London staff received an average of £2,318,181 annually in 2025, according to accounts for OpenAI UK Ltd. The 110 employees shared £87m in salaries and £168m in shares. This figure is 58 times the UK median earnings. OpenAI declined to comment on the figures, which come after recent AI safety concerns.
items.title: OpenAI London Staff Receive Record Average Pay Amid AI Talent War

items.summary: The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy sent the Liaoning carrier task group to the Western Pacific for training on Wednesday. The PLA Navy stated the activity aligns with its annual routine training plan to improve realistic training levels and mission execution capabilities. It added the deployment complies with international laws and is not directed against any specific country.
items.title: PLA Navy Sends Liaoning Carrier to Western Pacific for Training

items.summary: The 2026 AFL trade period featured a high-quality class of players, with 23 trades and seven free agency moves resulting in 30 players finding new clubs for the 2027 season. The Bulldogs emerged as the busiest club, acquiring four new players including Zak Butters. Conversely, Geelong and Hawthorn gained significant upside through proven talent acquisitions. The period also saw a strategic shift where clubs prioritized proven talent over uncertain young prospects due to compromised draft values. North Melbourne made a record trade for Nick Blakey, while Melbourne offered future picks in negotiations. The market remained active until the final day, with teams balancing immediate needs against future draft capital.
items.title: AFL Trade Period Analysis Highlights Star Moves and Draft Strategy Shifts

items.summary: The Victorian government has granted final approval for the Warracknabeal Energy Park, a 219-turbine wind farm in the state's west. The project, proposed by WestWind Energy, aims to become the largest in the Southern Hemisphere. Following state sign-off, the proposal now awaits final approval from the federal government. The facility is expected to generate 1.5 gigawatts of renewable energy.
items.title: Victoria approves largest southern hemisphere wind farm

items.summary: Queues of vehicles formed across Bali as residents faced fuel shortages. Officials attributed the delays to distribution issues and a tanker anchor problem rather than depleted stocks. Governor Wayan Koster urged calm, noting fuel remained available at depots. Pertamina confirmed additional supplies were scheduled to arrive between 14 and 17 October, with stations operating 24 hours a day, though queues persisted.
items.title: Fuel Supply Delays Spark Panic Buying and Queues in Bali

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron warned that student anxieties are being exploited politically and turned into unacceptable urban violence. While acknowledging legitimate concerns, he condemned the unrest. Student unions are organizing a nationwide protest for October 17. The government deployed 3,000 substitute teachers, yet students view these measures as insufficient. Since the movement began, over 6,800 people, mostly minors, have been taken into police custody.
items.title: Macron Warns Student Anger Exploited Amid France Protests

items.summary: Elon Musk stated that US government controls over Starshield dictate speed limits on Ukraine's Starlink network, which disrupted drone missions. While Ukrainian officials, including President Zelensky, suspect political motives behind the restrictions, Musk maintained that Starlink is for civilian use and Starshield is controlled by the US military. The US government has not commented on the matter.
items.title: Musk Attributes Starlink Speed Limits to US Government Control

items.summary: French anti-terror investigators have assumed control of an investigation into a school shooting near Marseille, following an initial probe that linked the 14-year-old suspect to the True Crime Community. Two teachers were wounded when a student fired a hunting rifle concealed in a guitar case. FRANCE 24 interviewed security consultant Alexandre Rodde, author of a report on nihilistic violent extremism and the True Crime Community in France.
items.title: French Anti-Terror Investigators Probe True Crime Community Link to School Shooting

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street, emphasizing Britain's enduring support for Ukraine five years into the conflict. Burnham stated the UK would "forever stand by you" and is accelerating air defence deliveries. The meeting, held at No 10 Downing Street with a ceremonial guard, aims to strengthen European alliances and repair ties with the United States.
items.title: UK Prime Minister Welcomes Ukrainian President to Discuss War Support

items.summary: Supporters gathered outside Rome's Gemelli Hospital to support Pope Leo XIV as he recovers from surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. Doctors report the 71-year-old pontiff is walking and eating with normal progress. Angele Bilegue, a visiting nun, expressed optimism, stating the cancer was caught in time and will be resolved soon. The Vatican has not yet announced biopsy results to determine if the cancer has spread.
items.title: Well-wishers Rally Behind Pope Leo XIV During Cancer Recovery

items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization states that El Niño is intensifying and likely to persist through February 2027. Regional forecasters predict a 90% chance of excessive rainfall in parts of Ethiopia, Somalia, and Kenya between October and December 2026, which could destroy crops and trigger floods. Action Against Hunger warns that failed harvests and funding cuts are already causing food shortages in Madagascar and Somalia, where 205 health facilities have closed. Rotimy Djossaya, the aid organization's chief impact officer, urges immediate action and flexible funding to help vulnerable communities, including children under five and displaced people, prepare before the crisis worsens. He emphasizes that waiting for disasters to occur often results in lost lives.
items.title: Experts Warn of Deepening Hunger in East Africa Amid El Niño

items.summary: The Supreme Court declined to hear a case brought by lobster fisherman Frank Thompson, who challenged Maine's requirement for commercial fishing boats to use electronic tracking devices. The court's denial allows the state to collect data for industry management and whale protection. While Thompson's legal team argues the measure violates Fourth Amendment protections, environmental groups and state officials support the surveillance as essential for conservation and enforcement.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Lobster Fisherman Challenge to Mandatory Boat Tracking

items.summary: The Forensic Science Laboratory unlocked a tablet, laptop, and one mobile phone belonging to deceased IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode, but an iPhone remains locked. Police await a detailed report to determine if a suicide note or final messages exist. Investigators have recorded statements from over 70 people and sought documents, including an alleged apology, while Sahil's parents stage a hunger strike alleging caste discrimination.
items.title: FSL Unlocks Devices in IIT Bombay Student Death Case While iPhone Remains Locked

items.summary: A Meerut court sentenced Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla to death for murdering Saurabh Rajput, a merchant navy officer. The couple, convicted of murder and evidence destruction, faced fines totaling ₹70,000 each. Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the sentence after 100 hearings involving 22 prosecution witnesses. The crime involved dismembering the victim's body and sealing it in a cement-filled drum.
items.title: Meerut Court Sentences Wife and Partner to Death for Husband's Murder

items.summary: Tonbo Imaging will open its IPO subscription on October 15, 2026, with a price band of Rs 665-700 per share. The offer for sale involves up to 1.21 crore equity shares, with proceeds going to selling shareholders. BlackRock, SBI MF, and other global and domestic investors participated in the anchor round, which saw strong interest from mutual funds and institutional investors.
items.title: Tonbo Imaging Opens IPO Subscription Amid Strong Anchor Interest

items.summary: Dr. Mitrabarun Ghosh, an Assistant Professor at Paari School of Business, stated that engineering and management graduates have diverse career opportunities across traditional industries, emerging technologies, and business leadership. Speaking at a career guidance session for final-year students, he emphasized that neither path is inherently superior and advised students to choose based on their interests and long-term aspirations while considering factors like institutional rankings and return on investment.
items.title: Expert Says Engineering And Management Courses Offer Diverse Career Paths

items.summary: A false hijack alert diverted Air India flight AI2030 from Frankfurt to Jaipur, causing hours of delay for 306 passengers. Pilots denied squawking code 7500, pointing to a potential ATC software glitch. Security agencies cleared the aircraft and crew, with Air India expressing regret over the disruption. A probe is underway to investigate the incident involving Mumbai ATC's new systems.
items.title: Probe launched into false hijack alert on Air India flight

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is traveling to Mumbai and Jamnagar to tour the Reliance oil refinery. The State Department announced the visit, highlighting a focus on energy cooperation and strengthening the US-India strategic partnership. This trip follows tensions over regulatory delays and talent mobility issues, with India expressing concerns about US remarks and sanctions. Rubio will meet with Indian officials and business leaders to discuss enhanced economic and commercial opportunities.
items.title: Rubio Visits Reliance Refinery Amid US-India Strategic Partnership Push

items.summary: US AI shares fell sharply, erasing approximately $80 billion in market value as concerns over rising interest rates intensified. CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle, and Dell Technologies led the declines. Analysts noted that higher borrowing costs disproportionately affect unprofitable firms and that investors are becoming cautious about aggressive AI spending. While some executives dismissed market reactions as irrational, others highlighted the risks posed by long-term rates approaching 6%. The Nasdaq dropped 2%, with major hyperscalers also seeing losses.
items.title: AI Stock Declines Wipe $80 Billion Amid Rate Fears

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is visiting India from October 18 to strengthen energy cooperation and investment. While discussions on a bilateral trade agreement are expected, sources indicate a breakthrough before the November mid-term elections may be unlikely due to contentious tariff issues. The visit includes stops in Mumbai and Jamnagar, focusing on deepening economic ties.
items.title: Rubio visits India to boost energy and investment ties amid stalled trade talks

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that India-US trade negotiations are approaching a resolution, though clarity remains on how India fares against competing economies. He noted that while a bilateral trade agreement framework was announced in February, ongoing US tariff changes and Section 301 investigations have complicated the process. Jaishankar emphasized that both sides are still ironing out details and waiting on certain matters before a final deal can be made.
items.title: Jaishankar Says India-US Trade Talks Near Landing Point Amid Competitive Economy Concerns

items.summary: The Indian government has no plans to reduce import duties on pulses for now, Consumer Affairs Secretary Nidhi Khare stated. Officials rely on domestic crop prospects and global supplies to manage prices despite rising retail costs and uneven monsoon rainfall. The strategy involves the kharif crop and buffer stocks rather than lowering duties.
items.title: India Govt Keeps Import Duties on Pulses Amid Price Concerns

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that peace along the Line of Actual Control is essential for normalizing India-China relations, noting that border disturbances would impact bilateral ties. He linked trade expansion to stability but clarified that resolving the boundary dispute is not a prerequisite. Jaishankar also highlighted India's trade deficit with China and the lack of a level playing field, while China objected to India's naming of 28 Ladakh locations.
items.title: Jaishankar Links LAC Peace to India-China Economic Ties

items.summary: Security agencies in Rajasthan destroyed suspected RDX and detonators recovered from a drone drop near the India-Pakistan border. A Jaipur bomb disposal squad conducted a controlled operation after a joint search by the ANTF and BSF uncovered the consignment in Sri Ganganagar district. The explosives were detonated, and two suspects from Punjab have been arrested. Surveillance has been heightened in the region.
items.title: Security Agencies Destroy Drone-Dropped Explosives in Rajasthan

items.summary: Actor Jake Johnson has listed a contemporary Pasadena home for $3.295 million. The property features 3,153 square feet, four bedrooms, and four bathrooms, including a sunroom with a sauna and two detached structures. Thomas Atamian of Coldwell Banker Realty is handling the listing. The home was built in 1947 and remodelled in 2004 by architect Aleks Istanbullu. Media reports note the price may round to $3.3 million or $3.29 million.
items.title: Actor Jake Johnson Lists Pasadena Home for $3.295 Million

items.summary: The Social Security Administration projects a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, adding an estimated $75 monthly for beneficiaries. However, retirees and advocates argue the increase is insufficient against rising expenses for food, healthcare, and housing. While the adjustment covers nearly 72 million people, concerns persist that inflation and specific cost hikes, such as prescription drugs, will erode its value. Advocates highlight that the adjustment may not fully reflect older Americans' spending patterns, particularly regarding medical costs, leaving many financially insecure despite the nominal increase.
items.title: Social Security COLA 2027 Increase Falls Short for Retirees Amid Rising Costs

items.summary: The Indian government and Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) sold a combined 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank to an arm of Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore. This transaction, cleared by the cabinet committee, helps the government meet its Rs 80,000 crore disinvestment target. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated the deal involves strategic restructuring, allowing the government to retain a 15% stake while enabling the bank's growth through foreign direct investment.
items.title: Government and LIC sell IDBI stake to Fairfax for record FDI

items.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation arrested the Executive Director of Munitions India Limited and two others in a bribery case. Searches at the accused public servant's premises in Pune recovered Rs 1.73 crore in cash. Further searches in Mysuru, Bengaluru, and Delhi yielded Rs 50 lakh in cash and documents. Allegations include demanding illegal gratification for favours and leaking sensitive defence information.
items.title: CBI Arrests MIL Executive And Others In Bribery Case

items.summary: The Supreme Court of India directed the Election Commission of India to produce available records regarding the 2023 Sringeri vote count, warning of an adverse inference for failure to do so. The court expressed surprise at the ECI's inability to trace the footage during a dispute over the constituency's election result. The matter was posted for a hearing on February 15, 2027. This dispute arose after a recount of postal ballots changed the declared winner from Congress leader TD Rajegowda to BJP candidate DN Jeevaraj in May 2026.
items.title: Supreme Court Warns ECI Over Missing Sringeri Poll Footage

items.summary: Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Lieutenant-Governor of Delhi, argues that electric mobility represents a broad transformation essential for India's strategic and ecological goals. He highlights the need for an integrated ecosystem involving energy, manufacturing, and recycling. Sandhu notes that while government initiatives like the PM E-DRIVE scheme provide support, success depends on accessible infrastructure and citizen-centric solutions. He emphasizes Delhi's role in leading this transition through innovation and sustainable urban planning.
items.title: Taranjit Singh Sandhu Advocates for Electric Mobility Transition in India

items.summary: NACOF India Ltd. issued a legal notice to BRS leader RS Praveen Kumar, demanding he withdraw allegations regarding the TGSWREIS tender within seven days. The federation, which won the May 2026 tender for food and cleaning supplies in Telangana, called the claims baseless and threatened civil and criminal proceedings if he fails to comply by removing related content and issuing an apology.
items.title: NACOF Issues Defamation Notice to RS Praveen Over Tender Allegations
